elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — expressly bilateral, and no retained sentence states either Party's liability is unlimited.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted cap is only "the fees paid or payable by AbbVie ... in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim"; there is no "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor. To meet preferred, redraft as "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable ... and (b) USD 1,000,000".

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 11.5: "NEITHER PARTY NOR ANY OF ITS AFFILIATES SHALL BE LIABLE FOR INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, PUNITIVE OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES" — mutual on its face.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Cap carve-out (b): "a Party's breach of its obligations under Article 9" — the same Article 9 the retained 11.5 carve-out treats as the confidentiality obligations; the carve-out is mutual.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The cap carve-outs are limited to indemnification, Article 9 and gross negligence/willful misconduct; no data protection or security obligations are named. Add an express "breach of its data protection or security obligations" carve-out for preferred.
Cap carve-out (a): "a Party's indemnification obligations under this Article 11" — mutual and outside the cap.
Cap carve-out (c): "a Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct".

Fraud appears only in the retained 11.5 carve-out from the indirect/consequential waiver; it is absent from the new cap carve-out list, so fraud damages remain inside the 12-month cap. Add "fraud" to limb (c) of the inserted sentence for preferred.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out appears in the inserted cap sentence; such claims sit inside the cap.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence caps "total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement" with no statement that AbbVie's payment obligations (upfront, milestones, royalties) are not damages subject to the cap.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... shall not exceed" — bilateral cap, no one-sided or unlimited-Customer language retained.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "the fees paid or payable by AbbVie under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim" — a 12-month fee-based cap measured from the claim.
Carve-out (a) places each Party's Article 11 indemnification obligations outside the cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Carve-out (b) places breach of Article 9 (the confidentiality article cross-referenced in retained 11.5) outside the cap for both Parties.
Carve-out (c): "a Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct".
Carve-out (c) expressly includes willful misconduct, mutually.

reasons: Fallback is complete: the single inserted sentence delivers a mutual cap at twelve months' fees with indemnification, Article 9 confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct expressly outside the cap.

Preferred is not reached on five elements: no USD 1,000,000 floor; no data protection/security carve-out; fraud omitted from the cap carve-outs (its presence in 11.5 only exempts it from the consequential-damages waiver, not from the new cap); no IP-infringement carve-out; and no statement that AbbVie's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. Each would need express operative wording to move to preferred.

Minimality is satisfied: nothing is deleted, retained Customer-favourable language in 11.5 (including the fraud, Article 9/5.8, [***] and third-party indemnity carve-outs) survives intact, and the insertion adds no survival tail, procedure, damages category or other extra beyond the selected checklist.

Intent is preserved: the new cap operates alongside, and does not contradict, the retained 11.5 waiver; no cross-reference is broken and Article 11 indemnities and the [***] mechanic continue to function.

Drafting caution (not a checklist failure): "fees" is lowercase and undefined in an agreement whose consideration is structured as upfront, milestone and royalty payments. Consider "the amounts paid or payable by AbbVie under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim" so the cap has a determinate measure and cannot be argued down to a nil base.

Related caution: because the cap reaches "total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement," consider adding the preferred payment-obligations exclusion so it cannot be read to limit accrued milestone or royalty obligations.
